advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Cache/share the built corpus + loaded cache rows between `_select_rows` and `_material_index` (and across criteria) rather than rebuilding per attempt.
evidence: _select_rows: `manifest = corpus.build_corpus({"default": tracker}, cache_dir=cache_dir)` then `_load_cache_rows`
_material_index: `manifest = corpus.build_corpus({"default": str(config.tracker_dir(repo_root))}, cache_dir=cache_dir)` then `_load_cache_rows` — same cache_dir `.rebar/fixture_heal_cache`
`_ProductionAttempter._criterion_rows` memoizes select rows per criterion, but `_material_index` is rebuilt on every `run` via `_run_admission`

heal.py:404 `_select_rows` does `corpus.build_corpus({"default": tracker}, cache_dir=cache_dir)`, `fixture_selection._load_cache_rows(...)`, `fixture_selection._review_findings(tracker)`, `for review in reviews: review["findings"] = ...`, `fixture_selection._enrich_escaped_batched(reviews, tracker)` — full-corpus work then `select_candidates(reviews, criteria_ids=[criterion_id], ...)` filtered to one criterion
heal.py:478 `_material_index` again runs `corpus.build_corpus({"default": str(config.tracker_dir(repo_root))}, cache_dir=cache_dir)` and `_load_cache_rows(...)` over the whole corpus
heal.py:383-386 `_criterion_rows` memoizes only per criterion_id, so nothing is reused across the per-criterion loop at heal.py:196 `for criterion_id in attempted:`

The attempt list is `_default_criteria(...)` gap criteria (heal.py:301-306); both the criteria set and the regression corpus grow with the project, so the whole-corpus passes are redone once per criterion.
advisory.finding: `_select_rows` and `_material_index` each independently call `corpus.build_corpus({'default': tracker}, cache_dir=cache_dir)` and `fixture_selection._load_cache_rows(...)` on the same cache_dir per criterion attempt, duplicating the corpus build/load work. For a multi-criterion sweep this repeats the O(store) corpus assembly twice per criterion with no shared result.
merged_from: The heal loop reprocesses the entire regression corpus once per gap criterion: for each criterion in the attempt list, _select_rows rebuilds the corpus (corpus.build_corpus), reloads all cache rows, recomputes review findings, and re-enriches every review, and _run_admission separately rebuilds the corpus again via _material_index — all to filter down to a single criterion_id. Cost scales as O(num_criteria x corpus_size).
scenarios: A sweep with many gap criteria rebuilds the material index (full corpus load) once per admission run

advisory.finding: The `_record_spend` fallback branch — `usage_rows` present but `ledger.finalize` raises `UnpriceableRun`, so it swallows the exception and charges the pre-flight estimate instead — is never exercised. Every heal test that supplies rows (`admitted()` -> `usage_rows=(usage_row(),)`) installs a priceable `genai_prices` stub via `stub_prices`, so `finalize` always succeeds; `test_empty_usage_rows_still_fail_closed_on_budget` passes `usage_rows=()` and skips the `if usage_rows:` block entirely. Deleting the `except ledger.UnpriceableRun: pass` clause (or the trailing `charge_estimate`) would leave the loop recording nothing / raising on an unpriceable attempt with no test failing.
merged_from: `_ProductionAttempter.run`'s ADMITTED and SKIPPED_UNBALANCED classification branches are untested. The production-attempter unit tests (`test_incomplete_admission_is_not_a_reproduction_failure`, `test_unminable_drift_outranks_reproduction_failure`) only drive the `incomplete` and `unminable`-drift branches; `_stub_admission` hard-codes `_emitter_skips_unbalanced -> False`, so the `if _emitter_skips_unbalanced(...): return AttemptResult(SKIPPED_UNBALANCED)` line and the `if criterion_id in summary.admitted: return AttemptResult(ADMITTED)` line are added code with no direct assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that supplies usage_rows with a model the stubbed pricer rejects (LookupError) and assert ledger_total equals the pre-flight estimate for the tier/sample_n.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid re-reading/parsing the full ledger on every per-criterion reserve within a sweep (compute running spent once and track incrementally).
evidence: heal.py:196-201 `for criterion_id in attempted:` calls `ledger.reserve(..., ledger_path=str(ledger_file), cap_usd=cap_usd, reserve_usd=0.0)` each iteration

ledger.py:104 `spent = _spent_so_far(ledger_path)` and ledger.py:82-83 `_spent_so_far` -> `_read_ledger` which at ledger.py:76-77 does `[json.loads(line) for line in handle if line.strip()]` — a full re-read+parse of the whole JSONL each call
_record_spend appends one line per attempt (heal.py:257 charge_estimate / heal.py:245 finalize), so the ledger grows every sweep and each subsequent reserve re-parses a longer file
advisory.finding: ledger.reserve re-reads and JSON-parses the entire ledger file on every iteration of the per-criterion loop via _spent_so_far, so ledger read cost scales as O(num_criteria x ledger_lines) per sweep.
scenarios: Many gap criteria per sweep combined with a ledger that accumulates a line per attempt across many prior sweeps
advisory.suggested_fix: Read the ledger total once at the start of the sweep and maintain the running spent in memory as each attempt is charged, passing it into a cap check rather than re-parsing the whole JSONL file per criterion.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the loop's `_record_spend` charge against `run_admission`'s own `finalize` entry so an admitted criterion is not billed twice on the shared ledger (e.g. skip charge_estimate when an `admission-<prompt_id>` entry already exists, or have the loop not double-book).
evidence: heal.py `_record_spend`: `ledger.charge_estimate(run_id, tier, criterion_id, ledger.estimate(tier, sample_n), ledger_path=str(ledger_file))` with run_id `heal-<prompt_id>`
fixture_admission.py:224: `ledger.finalize(f"admission-{prompt_id}", tier, criterion, sample_n, ...)` on admit — same `ledger_path`
The production solver returns `fixture_admission.CaseOutcome(fired=..., usage_rows=[])` (heal.py:462), so `_record_spend` always takes the charge_estimate fallback, never finalize
dropped.finding: For a criterion admitted via the production attempter, two ledger entries are written to the SAME ledger file per attempt: `fixture_admission.run_admission` calls `ledger.finalize('admission-<prompt_id>', ...)` on admit, and the heal loop then calls `_record_spend` which (because the production solver always returns `usage_rows=[]`) writes a second `charge_estimate('heal-<prompt_id>', ...)` entry. The pre-flight `ledger.reserve` in the loop and the reserve inside `run_admission` both read cumulative `spent` from this same file, so the two entries compound: the loop's estimate is charged on top of the admission run's own reservation/record for the identical work.
scenarios: A live heal run admits several criteria; each admitted one is billed both an admission finalize entry and a heal estimate entry, so the cap is reached after roughly half the true budget
